title: Development of a rapid and efficient protoplast isolation and transfection method for chickpea (Cicer arietinum)
author: Cheng, Nakata
materials: Critical: High concentrations of purified supercoil plasmid DNA are crucial for protoplast transfection. Using commercial plasmid DNA purification kit, like QIAGEN kits, is recommended.3.Protoplast isolation from chickpea leaves(1)0.5 g of fully expanded leaves was harvested from 2 to 3 week old chickpea seedlings (Fig. 1B).

steps.title: Grow chickpea plants
steps.instruction: Sow 4–6 CDC Frontier chickpea seeds in 16 cm pots containing Pro‑Line commercial soil (C/20, Jolly Gardener, Oldcastle Lawn & Garden, ME, USA). Grow in a greenhouse under a 16 h light/8 h dark photoperiod, light intensity 686–1400 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹, at 26 °C day / 18 °C night for 2–4 weeks, ensuring plants remain healthy and free of biotic or abiotic stress.

steps.title: Prepare plasmid DNA
steps.instruction: Transform E. coli TOP10 with the desired construct (pRTL2‑GFP, pRTL2‑GFP‑CXIP4, or pRTL2‑AtGrxS16‑GFP). Grow a 20 mL LB culture with 100 µg mL⁻¹ ampicillin in a 100 mL flask at 37 °C, 160 rpm shaking for 14 h until OD = 2.0. Purify plasmid using the QIAprep Spin Miniprep Kit and adjust the DNA concentration to 0.5 µg µL⁻¹ for transfection.

steps.title: Isolate protoplasts from leaves
steps.instruction: Harvest 0.5 g fully expanded middle‑position leaves from 2–3 week‑old seedlings. Cut leaves into 0.5–1.0 mm strips and place them in a petri dish with 5 mL freshly prepared digestion solution. Vacuum infiltrate for 20–30 min at room temperature, then incubate with gentle shaking (50 rpm) under low light for 2–3 h. Monitor digestion microscopically and stop by adding 5 mL W5 solution, followed by filtration through a 70 µm nylon mesh. Transfer filtrate to a 14 mL round‑bottom tube and centrifuge at 100 × g for 4 min (room temperature, low acceleration/deceleration). Remove supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 10 mL cold W5 (add 1 mL along the tube side, rotate, then add remaining 9 mL) and keep on ice for 30 min. Count protoplasts with a hemocytometer. Assess viability by mixing 5 µL PI stock and 4 µL FDA stock into 1 mL 0.55 M mannitol, adding 10 µL of each dye to 20 µL protoplast suspension, and visualizing by confocal microscopy. After the 30 min ice incubation, centrifuge again at 100 × g for 4 min, remove W5 gently, and resuspend the pellet in MMg solution to 1 × 10⁶ protoplast mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Transfect protoplasts with PEG‑calcium
steps.instruction: Aliquot 200 µL of the protoplast suspension (2 × 10⁵ protoplasts) into 14 mL round‑bottom tubes; set aside one tube as a negative control. Add 10 µL (5 µg) or 20 µL (10 µg) plasmid DNA to each tube and mix gently. Slowly add 210 µL (for 10 µL plasmid) or 220 µL (for 20 µL plasmid) freshly prepared PEG‑Calcium solution down the tube side and rotate gently. Incubate in the dark at room temperature for 15 min. Add 950 µL W5 solution slowly, mix, then centrifuge at 100 × g for 4 min (room temperature) and remove supernatant carefully. Resuspend the transfected protoplast pellet in 1 mL WI solution.

steps.title: Incubate and harvest protoplasts
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 5 % (v/v) sterile calf serum to each well of a 12‑well tissue‑culture plate, incubate 1 min, then aspirate the coating solution. Transfer the transfected protoplast suspension from each tube into the corresponding well, cover the plate and seal the lid with surgical tape. Incubate at room temperature in the dark for 12–18 h (protoplasts remain viable ≥24 h; 16–18 h gives stronger fluorescence). Harvest by transferring the culture to 14 mL round‑bottom tubes, centrifuge at 100 × g for 4 min, remove most supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in the residual supernatant using a wide‑end pipette.

steps.title: Image fluorescent signals
steps.instruction: Place 50 µL of the harvested protoplast suspension onto a glass‑bottom dish, cover with a glass coverslip, and image with a Leica SM8 confocal laser‑scanning microscope. Detect GFP or FDA emission at 510 nm (excitation 488 nm), PI emission at 582 nm (excitation 543 nm), and chlorophyll emission at 660 nm (excitation 633 nm).

description: Reliable transient expression systems have proven invaluable in the study of gene expression, gene function, protein localization, and protein–protein interactions. Such expression systems are especially important in plants, such as chickpea, that lack a simple and efficient method of stable plant transformation. Thus, we report here the establishment of a fast and reliable protocol for transient gene expression in chickpea. With the recent advances in chickpea genome sequencing [3,4] such a protocol is needed to help expedite efforts in gene discovery and crop trait improvements.
